thread:
mike_oncall: incident-bot page: High p99 latency on /v1/stream (payments flow) — >50% of streaming requests saw stall >10s. Paging on-call.
incident-bot: ALERT: service: inference-streaming | metric: p99_latency | value: 12.4s | threshold: 8s | hosts: gpu-proxy-12,gpu-proxy-15
mike_oncall: I'm on it. Noting customer-visible impact: payment confirmation step may hang for some users. @carla_support can you surface any support tickets? :eyes:
carla_support: seeing 3 chat threads in the last 12m reporting “payment never completed, spinner” for two customers (acme-pay, microfin). Adding their ids to the ticket.
jess_prod: adding context — rollout of a config change to the streaming proxy rolled 6m ago (keepalive/flush adjustments). Could be related. @dina_platform any deploys around that time?
dina_platform: deploy-bot shows a config rollout at 1958880000 -> proxy-stream-flush:0.5s -> was 0.2s. Rollout completed 1958880100. I did not get any pre-announce for this change. Reverting is possible but will need 2-3m to stage.
sam_sre: can we repro locally? logs show repeated backpressure on the downstream websocket with socket write stalls. Example from gpu-proxy-12:
```
W timeout flush chunk: conn_id=0x7f3a4, bytes_pending=16384, last_write=9.1s
client-backpressure: window=0
```
sam_sre: looks like clients with slow consumers cause the proxy to batch bigger chunks which then hits the p99 tail. Also certain clients stop acknowledging chunk frames.
mike_oncall: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) revert the flush config to 0.2s (fast), 2) enable per-conn small-chunk-mode, 3) switch affected payment route to non-streaming sync fallback. Which is lowest-risk and fastest?
jess_prod: 3) is app-level but fastest behaviorally: we can flip a routing flag to force non-streaming for /v1/stream? Probably needs a model fallback route — might be a 1-2m config toggle via console. 1) is risky but quick if staging pass is ok.
dina_platform: I can roll back flush to 0.2s immediately on the dedicated proxies. Rolling to staging first (1958884200) then prod (1958884320) — will take ~4m total. Confirming impact window.
carla_support: customers are requesting immediate mitigation — acme-pay is on a live batch run now.
incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff in 20m to night team. Page channel updated.
mike_oncall: I'll run the rollback now. @sam_sre monitor tail p99 and open sockets. @jess_prod start config for route fallback as plan B.
sam_sre: watching metrics -> starting live log tail on gpu-proxy-12/15. p95 stable, p99 climbing to 11-13s, error rate not increased but timeouts up.
(2m later)
dina_platform: rollback staged at 1958884980 -> flush=0.2s applied to canary proxies. Observing canary metrics.
sam_sre: canary p99 dropped from 12.2s -> 3.1s within 30s. Good signal.
dina_platform: rolling to prod now 1958885100.
(3m later)
sam_sre: prod p99 dropping to ~2.8s. Some clients still seeing trailing stalls — likely stuck connections that need reconnection. Suggest force-close old idle connections older than 60s.
jess_prod: I'll enable route fallback for payments while we finish cleanup. Flipping flag -> affected sessions will re-establish via sync endpoint. Doing it now.
jess_prod: flipped route -> verified that new requests are served non-streaming with fast responses. :white_check_mark:
carla_support: acme-pay reports improved behavior for new requests, but they still have 5 users in stuck state — advising to refresh session.
mike_oncall: good. Next steps: 1) force-close sockets >60s 2) schedule postmortem 3) add automated detection to block flush config changes without canary metric check for streaming p99.
sam_sre: force-close pushed: closed ~420 stale connections across proxies. That cleared most of the stuck sessions.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. p99 back under 3s; customer impact limited to earlier window. Escalation complete.
mike_oncall: creating incident ticket and assigning follow-ups: triage-owner=jess_prod, infra-fix=dina_platform, postmortem=sam_sre. ETA for postmortem doc by EOD tomorrow.
jess_prod: notes for postmortem: root cause likely flush-interval regression + slow-consumer amplification + lack of canary signal for p99 during config rollouts. Recommend gating flush config changes behind streaming p99 runbooks and a canary with synthetic slow consumers.
carla_support: I'll follow up with acme-pay and microfin, offer SLO credits if needed and collect session ids for audit.
mike_oncall: thumbs. Document timestamps for SOC: start=1958884327, mitigation-start=1958884980, resolved=1958890123. Handing off to night team for monitoring. Thanks everyone. :heart:
